Facet should become a full decision workspace with presentation quality that exceeds Lavish and review functionality that goes materially further. The goal is not decorative HTML volume: it is modular creative composition, excellent interaction design, durable collaboration, and substantially lower Codex usage. The product promise is: turn compact agent intent into a premium adaptive workspace, guide people from evidence to decision, then return precise feedback as tiny semantic changes.

title: Design reference — shadcn principles, Facet identity
text: Use shadcn/ui as a quality reference for composable accessible primitives, thoughtful defaults, calm neutral surfaces, disciplined spacing, clear component states, responsive sidebars, dialogs, sheets, tables, charts, and command interfaces. Do not clone its site or make shadcn a runtime requirement. Facet should translate those principles into dependency-light semantic renderer primitives and retain its own violet-and-cyan identity, review modes, local-first security boundary, and artifact protocol.

title: Color direction — neutral precision with expressive signals
text: Adopt a shadcn-inspired neutral foundation so content, evidence, and decisions carry the visual weight. Keep color purposeful: violet for primary action and active review state, cyan for keyboard focus and live location, and semantic colors for outcomes. These are proposed tokens and must pass automated and manual contrast checks before implementation.

rows: Primary actions, selected anchors, Decide mode
Outcome states reinforced by icon and text

title: Modular composition system
text: Build the UI as replaceable layers. Primitives guarantee accessibility and states; semantic blocks express review meaning; layout recipes compose blocks for a task; visual lenses let the user change perspective without regenerating content. Each layer remains deterministic and locally rendered so visual richness costs almost no additional model output.

data.summary: Design tokens feed accessible primitives, semantic blocks, adaptive recipes, and user-selectable review lenses

Review primitives — anchor, thread, change marker, evidence badge, decision action

title: Functionality beyond Lavish
text: Facet should pair premium composition with capabilities that improve the complete decision lifecycle. The differentiator is not the number of components; it is how evidence, discussion, change, and commitment remain connected.

title: Creative interaction ideas
text: Add a Decision Cockpit that condenses recommendation, unresolved risks, confidence, and next action into one focused surface. Introduce Evidence Gravity so strongly supported claims visually gain weight while uncertain assumptions remain visibly provisional. Offer Story mode for guided presentation, Board mode for spatial comparison, and Focus mode for deep reading from the same artifact. Add a Revision Radar that highlights semantic change by importance, a Devil's Advocate lens that foregrounds counterarguments already present in the artifact, and a Token Receipt that shows the cost of initial creation and each revision. These experiences must be derived from structured data—not generated decoration—and must remain readable without animation or color.

title: Visual acceptance pack for the proof sprint
text: The first implementation increment is complete only when one end-to-end review demonstrates the new design system and interaction depth across realistic states.

items: Desktop shell at 1440 and 1024 pixels with collapsible navigation and review rail
Tablet and mobile compositions at 768 and 375 pixels with a deliberate feedback sheet
Option Showdown recipe using modular comparison, risk, recommendation, and decision blocks
Explore, Review, and Decide states that are visually distinct without disabling comprehension
Empty, loading, saved, pending, failed, stale-anchor, conflict, offline, and resolved states
Light canvas and dark workspace themes with AA contrast and visible keyboard focus
Motion that explains selection and panel movement, with full reduced-motion behavior
Blind comparison against the Lavish reference using equal content and functionality

Stage 0 — Proof baseline: capture identical Facet and Lavish outputs, revisions, screenshots, timing, parity, and token estimates across five workflows.

Stage 1 — Design foundation: formalize the neutral-plus-violet token system and build accessible modular primitives inspired by shadcn's composability, without adding a mandatory framework dependency.
Stage 2 — Composition engine: ship executive brief, option showdown, and roadmap recipes plus summary bands, evidence clusters, scorecards, and premium decision controls.
Stage 3 — Review depth: add annotation pins, threads, guided review, evidence graph, change map, semantic before/after, decision rationale, and review lenses.
Stage 4 — Token compiler: shorten skill instructions, compile intent locally, apply defaults, validate automatically, and generate minimal patches, inbox digests, and token receipts.
Stage 5 — Creative expansion: add Story, Board, Focus, Decision Cockpit, Revision Radar, and only those semantic blocks validated by real workflows.
Stage 6 — Product proof: run blind visual-preference and task-completion studies, fix the largest failures, and claim superiority only after quality and efficiency gates pass.

Use the shadcn reference as a compositional benchmark: quiet neutral foundations, crisp typography, deliberate borders, confident control states, and modular blocks. Facet must exceed it through task-aware composition and integrated review intelligence rather than ornamental effects.
